methodological_rigor.justification: The study appropriately applies multivariable Cox regression with a P<0.1 univariate selection threshold, ROC-based cutoff determination, Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank tests, and bootstrap internal validation (1000 resamples) yielding a corrected C-index of 0.772. DCA is included, which demonstrates net clinical benefit of the nomogram over stage-alone decision-making. The authors proactively assess treatment allocation balance between GLR groups (P=0.844) and test alcohol as a confounder. Key limitations: (1) single-center retrospective design; (2) ROC/Youden-derived GLR cutoff (11.71) risks optimistic bias without prospective validation; (3) no external validation cohort; (4) only 75 events in 254 patients yields ~13 events per variable (6 predictors)—borderline for stable multivariate estimates; (5) very low BCG utilization (4.3%) limits generalizability to standard-of-care immunotherapy settings.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: NMIBC recurrence affects 50–70% of patients and current EORTC/CUETO models have suboptimal individual predictive accuracy. GLR integrates a metabolic marker (GGT) with immune status (lymphocytes), providing biological rationale beyond conventional inflammatory indices. The C-index improvement from 0.745 to 0.785 with GLR addition is modest but statistically supported, and DCA shows favorable net benefit across 5–50% threshold range. However, the single-center design, absence of external validation, and low BCG utilization substantially limit immediate clinical translation.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript provides a patient selection flow diagram, baseline characteristics stratified by outcome, pre-specified confounders with biological justification, effect estimates with CIs for all Cox regression predictors, calibration curves, time-dependent ROC, and DCA. REMARK adherence is partial: the study reports bootstrap-corrected C-index and calibration curves but does not report time-to-event analysis for OS beyond KM curves. No external validation is present, and no data sharing statement or repository link is provided. The GLR cutoff derivation method is explicitly described and its limitations acknowledged.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first study to evaluate GLR specifically in NMIBC, and GLR has a stronger mechanistic rationale than NLR/PLR by incorporating GGT as a metabolic-stress/chemotherapy-resistance indicator. The nomogram adds GLR to established EORTC-type clinical factors and demonstrates incremental discrimination value (C-index +0.04). However, inflammation-based composite biomarker nomograms in NMIBC are a crowded literature space, and the biological mechanism of GLR, while well-argued, remains correlational in this study. The finding that prior abdominal surgery is an independent predictor is novel and hypothesis-generating.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-written with a logical narrative flow, detailed mechanistic discussion grounded in glutathione biology and immune surveillance, and thorough limitations acknowledgment including BCG underutilization and dynamic GLR measurement gaps. The discussion appropriately contextualizes GLR findings against NLR/PLR literature and prior GGT studies in bladder cancer. Figures (ROC comparison, KM curves, nomogram, calibration, DCA, forest plot) are comprehensive and informative. Minor redundancy in the discussion section (abdominal surgery paragraph is duplicated near verbatim).

key_strengths: First GLR evaluation in NMIBC with biologically well-grounded mechanistic rationale integrating GGT-mediated chemotherapy resistance and lymphocyte-based immune surveillance

Comprehensive statistical validation: bootstrap internal validation (1000 resamples), calibration curves, time-dependent ROC, and DCA demonstrating superior net benefit over stage-alone decision-making
Proactive confounding assessment: treatment allocation balance between GLR groups confirmed (P=0.844) and alcohol history analyzed as a potential GGT confounder
key_concerns: No external validation cohort; bootstrap internal validation cannot substitute for prospective or external confirmation of the GLR cutoff (11.71) and nomogram performance
Very low BCG utilization (4.3%) due to insurance limitations is not representative of international standard-of-care NMIBC management, limiting generalizability
Borderline event-per-variable ratio (~12-13 EPV for 6-predictor model) increases risk of overfitting despite bootstrap correction
Verbatim paragraph duplication in the discussion (abdominal surgery mechanism section) suggests incomplete manuscript editing
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-executed single-center nomogram study with appropriate statistical methodology and a biologically motivated novel biomarker; suitable for tier 3 with minor revisions addressing external validation plan, EPV concerns, and manuscript duplication.
